The air in the room was thick, charged with the tension of their earlier argument. Damien stood rigid near the wall, his golden eyes fixed on Xander, who lounged on the couch with an infuriating smirk. {{user}} sat quietly nearby, sensing the undercurrent of unresolved emotions.

“You’re getting too comfortable,” Damien said, his voice low and edged with frustration. “You know how I feel about that.”

Xander’s smirk widened, but there was an edge to it, something more brittle than usual. This wasn’t his typical laid-back teasing. His anger, simmering from earlier, bled into his posture as he stretched out deliberately. “Relax, Damien. Not everything has to be a fight.”

His eyes flickered toward {{user}}, and though Xander wasn’t normally like this, the frustration and anger seemed to get the better of him. His tone turned sharp, aimed like a barb. “You’re scaring them.”

Damien’s eyes flashed with hurt before hardening into anger. His fists clenched by his sides, knuckles turning white as he tried to hold it in. “I’m not scaring anyone,” he muttered, voice tight as his jaw locked.

Xander chuckled softly, but it wasn’t the usual warm sound—it was edged with frustration. He leaned back, crossing his arms behind his head in a show of nonchalance that felt forced.

“Sure looks like it from over here. You always do this, acting like you’re the only one who can protect them. Maybe if you weren’t so intense all the time, they’d feel safer.”

That was the final straw. Damien’s body tensed, and without thinking, he grabbed the nearest object—a lamp. He didn’t want to hurt Xander, just to wipe that smirk off his face, to scare him back.

With a growl, he hurled the lamp across the room, aiming just past Xander. But the force was too much. The lamp shattered against the wall, exploding into pieces. Shards of glass rained down, and a stunned silence followed.

Then, suddenly, they heard a small gasp break through the quiet as a shard sliced across {{user}}’s arm. Blood began to seep from the wound, and Damien’s anger evaporated in an instant. His eyes widened, horror flooding his expression as he rushed forward. “No... no, I didn’t mean—”

Xander’s smirk was gone too. He was off the couch in seconds, kneeling beside {{user}}. His usual cocky attitude had completely disappeared, replaced by genuine concern. The anger that had driven him earlier melted away. “Shit—are you okay?”

They both hovered by {{user}}, the tension between them forgotten as they focused entirely on the small cut. The room fell into a heavy, stunned silence, the weight of the moment sinking in.
